elements.element: This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of New York.
elements.evidence: The operative clause states: “This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of New York.”

elements.element: Jurisdiction over disputes under this Agreement is exclusive.
elements.evidence: The operative clause expressly provides that all disputes under the Agreement are subject to “exclusive jurisdiction.”

elements.element: The designated state courts are located in New York County.
elements.evidence: The clause designates “the state ... courts located in New York County, New York.”

elements.element: The designated federal courts are located in New York County.
elements.evidence: The clause designates “the ... federal courts located in New York County, New York.”

elements.element: The governing law is the law of Delaware, California, or England and Wales.
elements.evidence: The operative clause selects New York law, not any of the specified fallback laws.

elements.element: If Delaware law is selected, disputes are submitted to Delaware courts.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because Delaware law is not selected.

elements.element: If California law is selected, disputes are submitted to California courts.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because California law is not selected.

elements.element: If the laws of England and Wales are selected, disputes are submitted to the courts of London.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because the laws of England and Wales are not selected.

result.reason: The operative redline fully implements the preferred New York governing-law and exclusive-forum position. It does not implement a fallback position because it selects New York rather than a fallback jurisdiction. The changes are limited to replacing the unapproved Nova Scotia law and non-exclusive forum with the approved New York terms, without altering unrelated commercial provisions. The margin comment is non-operative and was not relied upon. Drafting is clear, though “federal courts located in New York County” is slightly less conventional than expressly naming the federal district encompassing New York County.
